summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing confidential supply-chain data, then building a general, agent-driven product (Lighthouse) that rechecks the launch plan on every portal drop, flags contradictions, and drives approved supplier actions.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses launch despite an 'all ok' plan (overbooked art-book receipt, failed statue lot, game-card airline offload) and built a polling, versioned, multi-agent pipeline with a role-based UI. Added roles, a Fixed today list, For you/All open tabs and a 'How we got here' case flow, merged to main with 360 tests passing, though main is unpushed and live not restarted just before the 12:00 hand-in.

repo: Confidential portal data lives only in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds the token and .env.example is committed with an empty token.
The portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip, with no webhooks; files get replaced under the same name, so change detection needs SHA-256 polling and a versioned store.
Team workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md exist; claim work with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
The API does not load .env on import, so new settings such as ASK_VIEWER_TITLE must be read via a helper that loads .env first.

Routine steps are validated against the trigger kind: 'Chase once' only works on routines watching messages awaiting an answer, 'Ask for a status' only on shipment watchers; the server rejects others with 'step N cannot be done on open decisions'.
Case flow reuses the exported connector and node components from FlowGraph.tsx so it matches the routine diagram and cannot drift.

The Lucas branch new-approach has a Pulse console that bypasses the duplicate-send guard and record-only demo mode, and duplicates the existing escalation loop plus card_alerts.py; only its 'read documents before verification' step is worth porting.
Routines call claude-opus-5-5 using the .env key, independent of ASK_LLM_PROVIDER.
Demo server runs with background off and emails record-only; preview servers should use a copy of the demo state, never live state.

code.finding: New 'How we got here' flow component built from each case's own evidence, trail, prediction, approval rule and options; steps missing from the data are omitted rather than invented.
Link connector and node box are exported and shared with CaseFlow.

recognize_changed and read_with_backend are the functions to port into runner.run_pipeline, before the verifier, with a skip when no model is configured and a try/except that keeps the last good state.

friction: Misread the request twice: replaced names with roles when roles were wanted in addition, and built a duplicate Pulse-style chat instead of the flow view.
The two-column snake layout in the case flow read right to left and confused users, forcing a redesign to a single column.
The first 'Fixed today' version used supplier reply fields and wrongly listed Boise's late 36,000 game cards.
'Chase once if no answer' appeared broken because the Add step menu offered steps invalid for the routine's trigger.
The portal login password ended up in Discord history, which is a risk.
The data has no title for Felix, so 'Senior Buyer' needed a config setting.
The 12:00 hand-in deadline left little time while many UI polish requests kept arriving.
